item.text: {"text":"Recent work supports adding item semantics, but does not establish the exact constrained approach. [ITS-Rec (2025)](https://www.mdpi.com/2079-9292/14/9/1748) incorporates BERT representations of titles, descriptions and reviews into sequential recommendation; reviews contribute most of its reported gains, limiting applicability here. [KGSCL (2025)](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S089360802500070X) explicitly distinguishes substitutes and complements through an item knowledge graph, using substitution for replacements and complementarity for insertions. Its relations come from Amazon metadata unavailable in this task; it does not demonstrate that titles and descriptions alone recover these distinctions.\n\nA plausible experiment—not a result established by these papers—is one BERT4Rec network combining learned ID embeddings with a small, randomly initialized title/description encoder, jointly optimized through masked-item prediction. Shared token embeddings and pooling offer an inexpensive starting point; a learned gate can regulate textual contributions. Fully mask both ID and text at prediction targets, and use appended-mask inference. This could share evidence about artists, genres, series or descriptive terms when present, but semantic similarity cannot establish complementarity, compatibility or specific musical/narrative qualities absent from the text. The search found no directly verified 2024–2026 demonstration satisfying all constraints: training from scratch, one BERT4Rec model, titles/descriptions only, and no relationship labels. Treat this as a validation hypothesis, retaining the fixed four-category macro HR@10 criterion."}
